### Two electrons 

I can see the following trajectories, and phase map as well as offset of the total energy of the system. I tried to fix it using a projection method that projects the state onto the mannifold defined by $H(\mathbb{x})=E$. The integration method is a Runge-Kutta order 9.
 

![$x_1=-1.5$, $x_2= 1.3$, $p_1=0.4$, $p_2=-0.2$, $T=10^5$.](figures/1D-boxed-chr-particles/explore/explore2_particles_in_box01.png)

![$x_1=-1.5$, $x_2= 1.3$, $p_1=0.4$, $p_2=-0.2$, T=$10^6$.](figures/1D-boxed-chr-particles/explore/explore2_particles_in_box03.png)

![$x_1=-1.5$, $x_2= 1.3$, $p_1=0.4$, $p_2=-0.2$, T=$10^6$ with projection onto manningfold and further option Vern9(lazy=Val{false}()).](figures/1D-boxed-chr-particles/explore/explore2_particles_in_box04.png)

The option setting lazy integration to false should be used ["If p is changed in a ContinuousCallback, or in a DiscreteCallback and the continuous solution is used after the full solution, then set lazy=Val{false}()."](https://docs.sciml.ai/DiffEqDocs/stable/solvers/ode_solve/).

### Poincarés reoccurence theorem

We want to make a statment on chaotic behaviour. It takes up from measuretheory. Meaning we have a measureable set $\mathcal{C}$ equipped with a measure $\mu:\mathcal{C}\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$. 
Then we would like to describe the concept of maps $T:\mathcal{C}\rightarrow \mathcal{C}$ such that 
$$\mu(T\mathcal{C})=\mu(\mathcal{C})$$
which captures the concept of an **invariant measure** under transformation induced by the map $T$. 

The goal is to try to understand the set that describes the notion of **escaping the measurable set** eventually
$$\mathcal{C}_0=\{x\in\mathcal{C}:T^nx \not \in\mathcal{C}| n\in\N\}.$$

We hope to get an understanding by defining a set that are in the measurable set $\mathcal{C}$ at first, but 
$$D_n=\{\}$$
